messages:

Cc: Anna Green <anna.green@rockwell.com>
Date: 2027-01-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick intro — on-prem K8s for model serving (constraints)

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As discussed, Rockwell is evaluating Redwood Private for a pilot that will run model inference inside our secure datacenter (no internet egress allowed by policy). High level constraints: we have a mixed rack of 8 GPU servers (A100 equivalent), 12 CPU-only servers, a SAN-based blockstore (iSCSI) for persistence, and a thin L2/L3 network with restricted egress — outbound only via a proxy.

Specific asks we've listed in the attached site inventory: node counts, switch topology, and a short firewall rule set we can share. Can you confirm whether Redwood Private can: 1) run without outbound internet (control plane over VPN to a management plane is OK), 2) use local NVMe on the GPU servers for KV cache / ephemeral token cache, and 3) support our SAN as the persistent blockstore (with snapshots and encryption)?

Also — expected uplift in ops effort for the first 3 months.

Thanks,
Samir
Director, Infrastructure — Rockwell Systems

Attachments: rockwell-site-inventory.xlsx, proposed-nodegrid-diagram.png

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

Date: 2027-01-18T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick intro — on-prem K8s for model serving (constraints)

Samir —

Thanks for the note and the attachments (received). Short answers up front: 1) Yes — Redwood Private supports air-gapped/on-prem installs with a customer-hosted control plane (we can run a narrow management tunnel to Redwood Ops if you want centralized updates). 2) Local NVMe as an ephemeral KV cache is supported and recommended for GPU nodes (we use local SSD for cache to keep token latency low). 3) We support SAN/iSCSI blockstores via CSI driver; snapshots + encryption via KMIP/KMS integrations are supported, though we'll need to validate your SAN driver (we have a standard checklist).

I CC'd Marissa (deploy ops lead) and Irene (network/preflight) to run a short preflight and produce a deployment blueprint and mutual action plan. We'll propose a node/slice layout and storage tiering options by EOD tomorrow.

Quick ask on your side: can you confirm whether the SAN exposes multi-attach volumes or if it is single-writer only? That affects PV design (shared RWX vs RWO for DB/State).

Best,
Rafael
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: rockwell-firewall-rules.pdf

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-18T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Rockwell preflight — initial notes

Team —

I skimmed the inventory and sketched a quick topology. Key constraints / risks for the pilot:
- Control plane connectivity: if full outbound is blocked we need a site-to-site VPN for control plane sync (we can run updates over an approved egress).
- Network segmentation: single VLAN for GPU rack; need clear nodeSelectors/nodeAffinity and strict NetworkPolicy to isolate control/management plane from customer workloads.
- Storage: SAN is iSCSI single-attach per LUN by default — that means cluster must expose RWO volumes for model artifacts and use hostPath/local PVs for cache.
- Backup & snapshots: if SAN supports snapshots via API we can wire them to our backup controller; otherwise add scheduled rsyncs to a remote backup target.

I'll prepare a draft nodepool layout: GPU-cache nodes (nvme local), GPU-serve nodes (attached to SAN for persistent models, RWO), CPU-serve nodes for preprocessing, and infra nodes (control plane + log/metrics stack).

Cheers,
Priyom

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir@rockwellsys.com>, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-19T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick intro — on-prem K8s for model serving (constraints)

Samir —

Following up with a technical checklist and the deployment pattern we'd recommend for your environment. Paste below — I'll attach a diagram with node labels shortly.

1) Networking & routing- Control plane: site-to-site VPN terminating in customer VPC segment -> management host(s). No outbound internet required; we recommend a bastion for updates (SSH jump/proxied).- Egress: configure proxy host with allowlist for Redwood Ops IPs if you want optional telemetry uploads.- MTU: verify jumbo frame support across AFA/TOE if you plan to use RDMA for GPU servers.- Firewall: allow the management/bastion to reach the cluster API server on 6443; allow kubelet health checks on 10250 within the management VPC.

2) Node pools & scheduling- Node pool names: gpu-cache (local-nvme, taint: node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu-cache:NoSchedule), gpu-serve (gpu + san access, tolerate gpu workload taints), cpu-serve (for preprocessing), infra (control plane + observability).- Taints/tolerations: separate cache-only workloads onto gpu-cache; model servers should mount SAN volumes via CSI driver and be pinned using nodeAffinity.- Autoscaling: use a cluster autoscaler with conservative cool-downs; GPU nodes typically scale by whole nodes.

3) Storage & IO pattern- Ephemeral cache: use local NVMe on gpu-cache nodes for LRU token/KV caches. Use emptyDir with size limits and node-local provisioner for fast allocation.- Persistent model artifacts: provision RWO volumes on SAN via CSI. If multi-attach is not supported, run one replica per model-serving node or introduce a shared NFS gateway (we can deploy an HA NFS proxy if you need RWX).- Snapshots/encryption: integrate SAN snapshots with your KMS (KMIP preferred). Encrypt at-rest using disk encryption keys; ensure Redwood's CSI snapshot controller has API access or we deploy a small adapter.

4) Observability & runbook- Keep token-level latency dashboards for KV cache hit ratio, SAN IO ops, and per-node GPU utilization.- Eviction policy: prioritize eviction of cache pods before model-serving pods; configure kubelet eviction thresholds for disk pressure on NVMe.

Next steps: Rafael/Marissa — can you propose a mutual action plan (MAP) with dates for site preflight, CSI validation, and a smoke deploy? Samir — we'll use the attached diagram to confirm rack-level placement.

Regards,
Irene
Senior Network Engineer — Redwood Inference

Irene / Rafael / Marissa —

Thanks — that checklist is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our infra team:
- SAN LUNs are single-writer RWO by default. We can add an NFS headnode if RWX is required.
- KMIP KMS is available via our HSM provider (we can open a management API).
- RDMA isn't enabled across all switches; we'll keep MTU conservative for now.

On timeline: we can do preflight next week (week of Jan 25). We'll attach a firewall change request for the bastion host and share a whitebox for the SAN API.

Two asks for Redwood: 1) a concise preflight checklist we can give to our datacenter ops team (one page), and 2) a recommended nodepool sizing table (node type, CPUs, RAM, NVMe size, expected model footprint) so we can provision hardware.

Thanks,
Samir

Subject: Re: Quick intro — on-prem K8s for model serving (constraints)

Samir —

Great — we'll turn the checklist + node-sizing table around by tomorrow morning. Attached here are two items: 1) a one-page preflight checklist for your datacenter ops (network, firewall, SAN test commands, KMS endpoints), and 2) a suggested nodepool sizing table for your inventory. Highlights:

- GPU-cache (x2 nodes per rack): 8x 1TB NVMe each, 64GiB RAM, 12 CPU cores. Use these for fast KV cache (LSM-style caches).
- GPU-serve (x2 nodes per rack): attached to SAN, 8x A100-class GPUs, 256GiB RAM, high-throughput NICs. Pods mount RWO volumes for models.
- CPU-serve (3 nodes): 32 vCPU, 128GiB RAM for pre/post processing pipelines.
- Infra (3 control-plane boxes): 16 vCPU, 64GiB RAM, dedicated to k8s control plane + logging and metrics.

Operational notes: we recommend an initial pilot with reduced replication (single model replica per GPU-serve node) and synthetic load testing. We'll run CSI validation on your SAN during preflight — if RWX is required later we can add an NFS gateway managed by Redwood.

I'll drop the one-pager and the table into the Drive link and ping your infra team separately with the preflight ticket.

Looking forward to the site preflight week of Jan 25.

Best,
Rafael
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
